text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-A busy day for Prime Minister Hariri in Moscow. Russia is willing to play a bigger role in the peace process.
-President Hrawi to hold a news conference tomorrow before an eight-member ministerial committee starts mulling the municipal election law after the cabinet withdrew it from parliament last week.
-Hizbollah and Israel's local militia allies in south Lebanon carried out a swap of captives brokered by the International Committee of the Red Cross.
-Bank of Beirut will begin trading its shares on the Beirut Stock Exchange on April 11.
-Revenues from taxation of property deals rose to $13,325,928 in March from $11,623,486 in March 1996.
-U.S. ambassador in Beirut Jones said: We have to create renewed confidence and faith in the peace process in order to push it forward.
